text: The user is enjoying 'The Handmaid's Tale' on Hulu, and as of 22 May 2023 had been using Apple TV+ for a few months and had just finished the series 'For All Mankind'.

The assistant recommended five shows similar to 'The Handmaid's Tale': 'The Power' (Amazon Prime Video), 'Westworld' (HBO), 'The 100' (Netflix), 'Colony' (Netflix) and 'The Man in the High Castle' (Amazon Prime Video).

The assistant recommended five shows for fans of 'For All Mankind': 'Counterpart' (Starz), 'Electric Dreams' (Amazon Prime Video), 'Altered Carbon' (Netflix), 'Travelers' (Netflix) and '3%' (Netflix), a Brazilian dystopian series.

The user asked about 'The Power' on Amazon Prime Video. The assistant said it is based on Naomi Alderman's novel, in which women develop the ability to release electrical jolts from their fingertips, and that the series had not yet been released as of 22 May 2023.

The assistant said Naomi Alderman's novel 'The Power' won the Baileys Women's Prize for Fiction in 2017, and that the TV series is produced by Amazon Studios and Reed Morano, known for her work on 'The Handmaid's Tale'. No release date had been officially announced, though it was expected in 2023.
The assistant listed the main characters of 'The Power' as Allie, Margot, Tatiana and Daniel, describing Allie as the face of the new world order and Margot as a wealthy, ambitious politician.

The assistant described 'Westworld' as an HBO sci-fi western set in a fictional theme park where guests interact with lifelike robots called 'hosts' in a simulated Wild West, and listed Dolores, Bernard, William and Maeve as main characters.

The assistant said 'Westworld' had received 22 Primetime Emmy nominations with 5 wins, 2 Golden Globe nominations and 2 Writers Guild of America Awards, and named Evan Rachel Wood, Thandie Newton, Jeffrey Wright and Ed Harris as standout cast members.

The assistant said 'Westworld' had three seasons totalling 28 episodes as of 22 May 2023, that a fourth season was confirmed with no release date announced, and that the show contains violence, nudity and graphic content.

The assistant said 'Westworld' is an HBO original and listed ways to watch it: an HBO subscription added to cable or satellite, the standalone HBO Max service, the HBO add-on through Amazon Prime Video, or buying individual episodes or seasons through Amazon Prime Video, Google Play, iTunes or Vudu.
The user decided to watch 'Westworld' through the HBO add-on on Amazon Prime Video, since they already had an Amazon Prime membership, and asked about its fees and restrictions.

The assistant said the HBO add-on on Amazon Prime Video costs $14.99 per month or $139.99 per year, is added to the user's Prime membership bill, and is available in the United States and certain U.S. territories.

The assistant said the HBO add-on allows streaming on up to two devices at the same time, that HBO Max allows up to five simultaneous streams, and that some HBO content such as certain documentaries or specials may not be available through Prime Video.

The assistant recommended five shows similar to 'Westworld': 'Black Mirror' (Netflix), 'Electric Dreams' (Amazon Prime Video), 'Altered Carbon' (Netflix), 'Colony' (Netflix) and 'Travelers' (Netflix).

The assistant recommended five shows similar to 'For All Mankind': 'The Expanse' (Amazon Prime Video), 'Farscape' (Amazon Prime Video), 'Killjoys' (Syfy), 'Dark Matter' (Netflix) and 'Counterpart' (Starz).
The user watched a documentary on Disney+ during a free trial in April 2023 ('last month' relative to 22 May 2023) and asked for help identifying it.
The user recalled a recent nature documentary, possibly a series, with stunning wildlife footage, probably produced by Disney, and a serious, educational but engaging tone.
The assistant suggested five nature documentaries as possible matches: 'Our Planet' (2019), 'Dynasties' (2018), 'Blue Planet II' (2017), 'Wild Yellowstone' (2020) and 'America the Beautiful' (2022).

The assistant said 'Dynasties' is a BBC series narrated by Sir David Attenborough about five endangered species, and that 'Blue Planet II' (2017), also narrated by Attenborough and focused on marine life, is available on Disney+.

The user said none of the assistant's suggestions sounded right, and recalled a well-made documentary focused on one specific type of animal, with amazing footage of animals in their natural habitats, which they thought they watched around the middle of the free trial.
The user recalled that the documentary focused on a fairly well-known mammal species, set in forests or mountains, or possibly both.

The assistant suggested three mammal documentaries as possible matches: 'Bear Witness' (2020), a Disney+ original series about bears; 'Elephant Queen' (2020), a Disney+ original following the matriarch Athena in Kenya's Masai Mara; and 'Giant Pandas' (2020), part of the Smithsonian Wild series.
The user thought the documentary probably focused on the daily lives of the animals, was probably a standalone film rather than a series, and had a serious tone that was still engaging and inspiring.

The assistant suggested three standalone films as possible matches: 'The Elephant Diaries' (2020), 'The Great Bear Rainforest' (2020) and 'Polar Bear: Spy on the Ice' (2020), which is part of the Spy in the Wild series.

The user suggested the documentary might have been a Disney+ exclusive, since they started a Disney+ free trial in April 2023, and asked the assistant to check whether the documentaries it had suggested were exclusives.

The assistant said 'The Elephant Diaries', 'The Great Bear Rainforest' and 'Polar Bear: Spy on the Ice' are not Disney+ exclusives, describing them as BBC documentaries available on Amazon Prime Video and YouTube.
The assistant named 'Bear Witness' (2020) and 'Elephant Queen' (2020) as Disney+ exclusive documentaries that might match the user's description.

The user has been starting seeds indoors under grow lights in their basement since 20 February 2023, including tomatoes, peppers and cucumbers, which were about 2 to 3 inches tall and doing well as of 10 March 2023.
The user planned to plant out their seedlings soon and asked the assistant for the average soil temperature in their area.
The assistant said most vegetables and flowers prefer soil temperatures between 55°F (13°C) and 75°F (24°C), with tomatoes at 55-65°F (13-18°C), and peppers and cucumbers at 60-70°F (16-21°C).
The assistant recommended hardening off seedlings by gradually exposing them to outdoor conditions over 7-10 days before planting them out.
The user lives in zip code 23456 and has been fertilizing their seedlings with a balanced fertilizer while keeping the soil moist but not soggy.

The assistant said zip code 23456 is in Virginia Beach, Virginia, where average soil temperature in late March to early April is around 48°F (9°C) to 52°F (11°C), and can fluctuate by 2-3°F (1-2°C) from day to day.
The assistant suggested warming the soil with organic mulch such as straw or grass clippings, black plastic or row covers, or a cold frame or hoop house.

The user asked whether it was too early to plant out their tomatoes, peppers and cucumbers given the average soil temperature in their area, and whether they should wait for the soil to reach a certain threshold.

The user was preparing a raised bed in their backyard by adding a 2-inch layer of compost and mixing it into the soil, hoping it would warm the soil, and asked whether compost makes a significant difference to soil temperature.

The assistant said a 2-inch compost layer might raise soil temperature by 1-2°F (0.5-1°C) at most, which could bring the user's soil to about 50-54°F (10-12°C), still below the optimal range for warm-season crops.

The assistant said compost warms soil through insulation, microbial activity and improved soil structure, and recommended combining it with mulch, black plastic or row covers, or a cold frame or hoop house.
The user had planted peas that were already sprouting and asked how best to support them, including whether to add a trellis or cage.
The assistant listed four pea support options: a trellis or cage (including a tomato cage), individual pea stakes, netting or chicken wire, and a bamboo or dowel tepee.

The assistant said bush peas need support once they are about 6-8 inches (15-20 cm) tall, while climbing peas need support as soon as the first tendrils appear, usually at about 2-3 inches (5-7.5 cm).
The user started marigold seeds that arrived on 3 March 2023, and they were already germinating by 10 March 2023.
The user planned to plant seedlings outside in their backyard soon and asked what temperature is ideal for doing so.
The assistant said tomatoes should go outside when soil reaches about 55-60°F (13-16°C), with daytime air around 65-70°F (18-21°C), and marigolds when soil reaches about 50-55°F (10-13°C).
The assistant advised waiting until the average last frost date for the user's area has passed, and hardening off seedlings over 7-10 days before planting them outside.
The user planned to transplant their seedlings, including the marigolds, into larger pots soon and asked how to do it without shocking them.

The assistant advised choosing new pots only 1-2 sizes larger than the current ones, with drainage holes, and watering the seedlings the day before transplanting to make the soil easier to handle and reduce stress.

The assistant advised transplanting in the morning or late afternoon, keeping the soil consistently moist but not waterlogged for the first week, and supporting marigolds so they do not topple over in their new pots.
The user has been using a potting mix of peat moss, vermiculite and perlite for their seedlings and reported that it is working well.

The assistant said the user's peat moss, vermiculite and perlite mix is a good starting point, and suggested adding 10-20% compost, reducing peat moss to about 20-30%, and using more perlite or vermiculite for drainage.
The assistant gave a sample adjusted potting mix of 20-30% peat moss, 30-40% vermiculite, 30-40% perlite and 10-20% compost, optionally with a balanced fertilizer such as 20-20-20 NPK.
The user was considering adding support for their marigolds as they grow and asked for DIY trellis or stake ideas.

The assistant suggested DIY marigold supports including a bamboo teepee of 3-4 stakes, a wooden lattice, a netting trellis, bamboo or dowel stakes, a repurposed tomato cage and a wire coat hanger stake.
The assistant recommended soft ties such as twine, wire or velcro strips to attach marigold stems, and placing supports near young plants so the stems grow up through them.
The user planned to support their marigolds with stakes and twine and asked whether to tie each stem individually or to use a twine grid connecting multiple stems.
The assistant recommended a hybrid approach for the marigolds: tie weaker stems individually to stakes first, then add a twine grid connecting stems once the plants are more robust.
The assistant advised that a twine grid should use sturdy twine, evenly spaced stakes, enough slack for growth, and regular checks so it does not constrict the stems.
The user was planning to make amigurumi toys for their niece and nephew and asked what hook size and yarn weight suit a small to medium-sized toy.

The assistant said small to medium amigurumi toys are typically made with a 3.5mm to 4.5mm hook (US E/4 to 7) and worsted (#4) or DK (#3) weight yarn, producing a toy about 6-10 inches (15-25 cm) in height or diameter.
The user had recently found a stash of 17 skeins of worsted weight yarn and wanted to use them up.
The assistant said worsted weight yarn is thicker than typical amigurumi yarn, producing larger, softer toys with fewer stitches, and suggested starting with a 5mm (US H/8) or 5.5mm (US I/9) hook.
The user was thinking of making fingerless gloves as gifts for friends and asked for advice on sizing them properly.

The assistant gave fingerless glove size guidelines by hand circumference and length: small 6-7 inches (15-18 cm), medium 7-8 inches (18-20 cm), large 8-9 inches (20-23 cm) and extra large 9-10 inches (23-25 cm).
The assistant advised measuring hand circumference just below the knuckles and glove length from the base of the wrist to the tip of the middle finger.
The user had already made a pair of fingerless gloves for their sister's birthday using worsted weight yarn from their stash and planned to make more as gifts.

The assistant said that when using the same yarn and hook for gloves of different hand sizes, the user should adjust the stitch count, use a stretchy ribbed or textured stitch, and add a small amount of ease.

The user planned to make more fingerless gloves with the same worsted yarn and hook size, adjusting the stitch count for different hand sizes, and also to make amigurumi toys from the same worsted yarn.
The assistant advised using an amigurumi hook 0.5mm to 1mm smaller than the one used for fingerless gloves, for example a 4.5mm or 4mm hook in place of a 5mm hook, to get a denser fabric.
The user decided to start their amigurumi toys with a 4.5mm hook and adjust as needed, and planned to make tote bags on their recently fixed sewing machine.
The user asked for tips on working with cotton prints and on keeping seams straight and professional-looking for the tote bags.
The assistant recommended pre-washing and drying cotton prints, using a walking foot, pressing seams as you go, and using a consistent 1/4 inch seam allowance for even, professional-looking seams.
The assistant suggested tote bag tips: use sturdy interfacing for structure, reinforce the straps, add a lining for a professional finish and topstitch the edges.
The user asked the assistant for a good recipe for a chocolate cake with caramel ganache frosting.

The assistant gave a chocolate cake recipe for two 9-inch layers, baked at 350°F (180°C) for 35-40 minutes, using 2 3/4 cups all-purpose flour, 1 1/2 cups granulated sugar, 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1 cup whole milk and 2 large eggs.

The assistant's caramel ganache frosting uses 1 cup heavy cream, 1 cup granulated sugar, 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, 1 teaspoon sea salt and 1 cup dark chocolate chips (at least 60% cocoa), chilled for at least 2 hours or overnight.
The assistant said the cake stays moist if the batter is not overmixed, and that the ganache can be reheated in the microwave in 10-second increments if it becomes too thick.
The user was planning a cake for a friend's birthday and wanted lemon-flavored suggestions similar to the lemon poppyseed cake they had made for a colleague's going-away party.
The assistant suggested six lemon cake ideas: lemon lavender pound cake, lemon blueberry cake, lemon curd cake, a twist on lemon poppyseed cake, lemon chiffon cake and lemon-ginger cake.
The user said the lemon lavender pound cake sounded interesting and asked for details on how to incorporate lavender into it.

The assistant listed three forms of lavender for the pound cake: 1-2 teaspoons of dried lavender buds, about 1/4 teaspoon of lavender extract for baking, or 1-2 tablespoons of homemade lavender syrup.

The assistant's lemon lavender pound cake recipe uses 1 1/2 cups (190g) unsalted butter, 1 3/4 cups (210g) sugar, 4 large eggs, 2 1/4 cups (285g) flour and 1 cup (240ml) buttermilk, baked at 325°F (165°C) for 55-60 minutes in a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
The user said they would not use lavender syrup or infused milk, planned to add dried lavender buds to the batter, and asked how much sugar to use and whether to adjust the lemon zest and juice.

The assistant suggested 1 cup (200g) granulated sugar and 1/2 cup (100g) brown sugar, 1 1/2 teaspoons grated lemon zest (instead of 2) and 1 1/2 tablespoons lemon juice (instead of 2), and about 1 teaspoon of ground dried lavender buds for the pound cake.
The assistant advised using culinary or food-grade dried lavender buds and grinding them in a spice grinder or mortar and pestle to release their oils and spread the flavor evenly through the batter.
The user said their lemon poppyseed cake had been a hit before and asked how to store the lemon lavender cake, whether at room temperature or in the fridge, and how long it would stay fresh.
The assistant said the lemon lavender pound cake keeps up to 3 days at room temperature (68-72°F or 20-22°C), up to 5 days wrapped in the refrigerator, and up to 2 months in the freezer.

The assistant advised cooling the cake completely before storing it, wrapping it tightly, keeping it in an airtight container, slicing it just before serving with a serrated knife and serving it at room temperature.
The user planned to serve the lemon lavender pound cake at a birthday party and said they would store it properly beforehand.
The user was thinking of baking a batch of chocolate chip cookies to bring to the birthday party and asked for tips on making chewy cookies.

The assistant recommended a mix of white and brown sugar, room-temperature butter, not overmixing or overbaking, and optionally adding 1-2 tablespoons of honey, corn syrup or Greek yogurt for extra chewiness.

The assistant's chewy chocolate chip cookie recipe uses 2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup unsalted butter, 3/4 cup white sugar, 3/4 cup brown sugar, 2 large eggs and 2 cups semi-sweet chocolate chips, baked at 375°F (190°C) for 10-12 minutes.
The user wanted to get a better handle on their finances, track their spending habits and create a budget, and was unsure where to start, as of 26 May 2023.

The assistant outlined a six-step budgeting process: gather financial documents, identify income, track every expense for one month, categorize expenses, analyze spending habits, then create a realistic budget.
The user had been using their credit card a lot and believed they spent heavily on luxury items in April 2023, including a designer handbag that cost $800.
The user said they wanted to start tracking their expenses and asked for budgeting app recommendations.

The assistant recommended six budgeting apps: Mint, Personal Capital, YNAB, Spendee, Pocketbook and Wally. Mint, Personal Capital, Spendee, Pocketbook and Wally are free, while YNAB is paid with a free trial, and all are available on iOS and Android.
The assistant suggested categorizing the $800 designer handbag as a luxury item or a 'want' rather than a 'need' when tracking expenses.
The user said they would try Mint, and that they had recently been frequenting high-end department stores such as Saks and Neiman Marcus a lot.

The assistant said that regularly shopping at Saks and Neiman Marcus can be costly and encourage impulse purchases, and suggested setting a monthly luxury budget, making a shopping list, considering cheaper alternatives and waiting 24 hours before buying.

The user had begun browsing H&M and Uniqlo for affordable stylish clothing and was considering canceling a monthly beauty box subscription that cost $50 a month, because they were not using most of the products.
The user had started buying beauty products at a discount store, finding similar products at a fraction of the cost of the beauty box.

The assistant suggested the cashback apps Rakuten (formerly Ebates), TopCashback and Ibotta, the secondhand sources ThredUp, Poshmark and local consignment stores, and the 30-wear rule before buying a new piece of clothing.
The user said they had been eating out a lot, wanted to cook more at home and try new recipes, and asked for meal planning and budget grocery shopping tips.

The assistant recommended planning the week's meals on the weekend, using affordable proteins such as beans, lentils or chicken breasts, cooking in bulk, and using the meal planning apps Plan to Eat or Yummly.

The assistant suggested grocery savings through shopping sales, buying staples such as rice, pasta and canned goods in bulk, shopping at discount stores or Aldi, and using Ibotta or Fetch Rewards for cashback.

The user said they felt stuck in a cooking rut, had no dietary restrictions, preferred relatively healthy and balanced meals, and wanted to try Korean or Indian cuisine, which they had heard is often affordable and delicious.
The user was considering meal prepping on weekends to make weekdays easier and asked for tips on getting started.
The assistant recommended starting meal prep with one or two meals a week, cooking bulk proteins such as rice, quinoa or lentils, portioning meals, and storing them in labeled airtight containers.

The assistant suggested the Korean recipes bibimbap, japchae and kimbap, the Indian recipes chana masala, saag aloo and vegetable biryani, and the cooking techniques stir-frying, braising and roasting.
